responsibility: Provides rustc’s concrete compiler driver implementation: it is the top-level orchestration layer that turns a process invocation into a compiler run, handling lifecycle concerns from argument intake through execution, diagnostics, and termination. The crate’s `lib.rs` is the central entry point that coordinates command-line processing, compiler/session and interface setup, callbacks, `--print` handling, pretty-print integration, logging, Ctrl-C and signal handling, ICE reporting, and final process exit behavior. `args.rs` performs the earliest stage of driver input handling by reading raw process arguments, validating Unicode, and expanding `@file` argument sources, including unstable shell-style argfile expansion, so the rest of the driver receives normalized inputs. `pretty.rs` supplies the driver’s pretty-printing backend for source text and internal compiler representations such as AST, HIR, MIR, stable MIR, and THIR, selecting print modes, acquiring compiler state, and formatting annotated output. `print.rs` provides panic-safe stdout output helpers used by the driver so informational printing does not rely on the standard printing paths and stdout failures become fatal compiler errors. `session_diagnostics.rs` defines the structured diagnostics specific to the driver, covering `.rlink` loading and validation problems, ICE-related notes, dump-path and flag guidance, and unstable-feature usage errors. `signal_handler.rs` installs the Unix SIGSEGV handler that helps the driver recover enough context to print backtraces, recognize probable stack overflows, and emit user guidance before process termination. Together, these pieces make `rustc_driver_impl` the crate that encapsulates how rustc is invoked and supervised as an executable compiler front end.
